sources.title: Official biography, journalism, political career and appointments through 2026
sources.findings: Read official biography through 2026: born June 1, 1975 Ijevan; YSU studies 1991–1995 not completed; journalism from 1992, Oragir founded 1998, Haykakan Zhamanak editor 1999–2012. 2009 surrender, January 2010 seven-year sentence over 2008 events, May 27, 2011 amnesty after under two years; no claim full sentence served. Civil Contract association 2013 and party from 2015 distinct. March 31, 2018 movement, May 8 parliamentary election as PM, October 2018 resignation/acting service, December election and January 14, 2019 reappointment; April 25, 2021 resignation/acting service, June 20 election and August 2 appointment; June 7, 2026 election and August 2 appointment. Government motive/prisoner-of-conscience language not uncritically adopted as independent adjudication. Awards and family status not separately verified or featured.

sources.title: Career record and explicitly incomplete university education
sources.findings: Read Yerevan Press Club career profile: explicit incomplete higher education, journalism section of philology faculty 1991–1995; newspaper editor chronology 1998–1999/1999–2012 and parliament 2012–2018. No journalism degree inferred from occupation. Official term details independently taken from government/presidency rather than broad 2018–present shorthand.

sources.title: Archived member biography: education, newspaper editorships and parliamentary service
sources.findings: Read archived National Assembly ID1260 biography: birth, university entry/withdrawal, Oragir and Armenian Times editorships, 2012–2017 MP through Armenian National Congress and Civil Contract founding membership from 2015. Historical member page not proof of current MP office. Different translations Civil Treaty/Civil Contract refer to the same party, not two organizations. No precise 2012 election day asserted from unread ID1123 preview.

sources.publisher: Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe
sources.title: Doc. 16486 rev: 2026 election results and observer conclusions
sources.findings: Read relevant sections of PACE Doc.16486 rev: June 7, 2026 poll; final CEC certification June 14; Civil Contract 49.75%/726819 votes and governing majority. Conclusions call process well-run with genuine choice while raising foreign pressure, confrontational rhetoric, opposition proceedings, public-sector pressure and campaign-finance transparency concerns. Do not conflate rounded official bio 49.7%, preliminary 49.8% and final 49.75%; not percentage of all citizens nor direct PM vote. Findings attributed to observers, not independent case-level proof of every allegation. Entire appendices and precinct records not audited.

sources.title: 2 August 2026 ceremony and decree appointing Pashinyan prime minister
sources.findings: Read presidency August 2, 2026 ceremony account: Vahagn Khachaturyan signed appointment decree following Civil Contract parliamentary faction nomination under constitutional article 149. Acting title before signature and appointed title afterward are procedural stages. Same calendar date as 2021 appointment is confirmed, not a copied-year assumption. No separate decree document authenticated beyond official announcement.

sources.title: Trilateral statement: ceasefire effective 00:00 Moscow time on 10 November 2020
sources.findings: Read full relevant 2020 trilateral statement: ceasefire effective 00:00 Moscow time November 10; positions, territorial returns, Russian peacekeeping and transport provisions. Timeline deliberately uses effective date, not ambiguous November 9/10 signature/publication/timezone shorthand. Original five-year peacekeeping provision is not a claim troops remain there in 2026 or that later conflict/displacement never occurred. No claim all provisions fully implemented.

sources.title: Washington Joint Declaration signed 8 August 2025, published 9 August
sources.findings: Read Azerbaijan presidency publication of Washington joint declaration: signed August 8, 2025, page August 9 at 00:30; Aliyev and Pashinyan with Trump witness. Foreign ministers initialled agreed peace/interstate-relations text; declaration explicitly calls for further signing and ultimate ratification. TRIPP planning respects stated sovereignty/jurisdiction principles and is not automatically a completed extraterritorial corridor. Declaration, initialling, formal treaty signature and entry into force distinct.

sources.title: 8 August 2026 message explicitly distinguishing initialling from signing and ratification
sources.findings: Read Pashinyan August 8, 2026 anniversary statement: explicitly says peace agreement initialled a year earlier still awaiting signing/ratification, border work pending, prospective TRIPP implementation. His claims that peace is already established/irreversible are political assessments, not independent guarantee or substitute for legal process. Profile dates pending status to this speech, not an unverified claim that nothing changed thereafter. Refugee-rights political remarks not adopted as legal determination.

sources.title: Completed Dublin meeting with Aliyev on 12 November 2026
sources.findings: Read complete relevant Armenia November 12, 2026 Dublin meeting announcement: Pashinyan and Aliyev actually met during ninth EPC summit; transport/trade/border delimitation/confidence measures and TRIPP railway/highway design. Planning, proposed grid connection and reported transit volumes are not independently audited completion; numerical cargo claim omitted. Not merely November 11 invitation/itinerary.

sources.title: 12 November 2026 counterpart account of Dublin peace and transit talks
sources.findings: Read Azerbaijan counterpart November 12, 2026 release confirming same completed Dublin meeting and agenda. This is counterpart official corroboration, not an independent civil-society implementation assessment. Neither announcement alone establishes a newly signed/ratified peace treaty or completed TRIPP infrastructure.

sources.publisher: Armenian Legal Information System — European Court of Human Rights
sources.title: Pashinyan v. Armenia, applications 22665/10 and 2305/11, 18 January 2022
sources.findings: Read Armenian legal-information-system reproduction of Pashinyan v. Armenia, applications 22665/10 and 2305/11, January 18, 2022: case facts and paragraphs 42–49 on insufficiently specified wrongdoing and violation of Article 11 peaceful assembly. Header deliberation December 14, 2021 differs from January 18, 2022 judgment date. Profile claims only read Article 11 conclusion, not an invented acquittal, damages award or finding on every protest participant. Full domestic files, later domestic annulment, Article 5 disposition and enforcement not audited.
